value_prop: The moment you ship a feature, an on-brand enablement video and one-pager are drafted, quality-checked, and routed for approval — so sales knows what shipped, where it fits, and how to sell it.
when_to_use: When engineering ships faster than sales can learn, and enablement never keeps up.
talking_points: Context is perishable — capture the feature's story at the source
The builder already knows who they're building for

Two directors — content and camera — make it premium

Human approves, then it publishes to YouTube, the enablement hub, and Slack

How Amplify works.

scenes.narration: So how does Amplify actually do it? Let's walk the pipeline, end to end.

scenes.html:
The core idea
Two directors. Not one.
📝
Content director
what it means · the story · the sales layer
🎥
Camera director
where the eye goes · when to zoom · what to spotlight
scenes.narration: Most auto-generated demos feel off because they conflate two jobs. So we split them. A content director decides what the feature means and what sales needs to hear. A camera director decides where your eye goes. Two directors — that's the difference.

🎥

scenes.narration: For the demo, Amplify doesn't record anything by hand. It reuses what's already there — the engineer's end-to-end test, or a clip from the pull request, which already drives the exact happy path. Then the camera director eases in and spotlights the action, so your eye always knows where to look.

footage.narration: Here's a real one. Customers kept asking to share a UiPath app publicly — no account, no sign-in. Now, in the app's properties, one checkbox makes it public. Run it, and it's live at a public URL anyone can open, ready to embed anywhere. Amplify cut this demo straight from the recording, and guided your eye.

scenes.narration: Every scene is generated fresh and on brand — title cards, diagrams, callouts, kinetic captions, charts, even code diffs — all built on the UiPath design tokens. Change a token, and every future video updates for free.

scenes.html:

It sounds produced.
VoiceoverMusic bed · duckedSFXSynced captions
scenes.narration: A natural, expressive voiceover. A music bed that ducks under the narration. Subtle sound effects on every transition. And captions, synced to the word. It sounds produced — because it is.

scenes.html:
Quality gates
It won't ship a lie.
  • ✓Deterministic render
  • ✓On-brand palette
  • ✓Renders clean
  • !Claim-check: “handles unlimited anonymous traffic” — not in the diff → sent to a human
scenes.narration: Before anything ships, it runs quality gates. On brand. Renders clean. And the big one — a claim check. If the narration says something the code doesn't support, like a made-up metric, it's flagged and sent to a human. It will not ship a hallucination to a customer.

scenes.narration: And from that one plan, you get two artifacts — the video, and a matching one-pager. Same story, so they never contradict each other. One to watch, one to skim.

youtube_metadata.title: Amplify — Feature → Enablement Pipeline (Hackweek Demo)
youtube_metadata.description: Engineering ships faster than sales can learn. The moment a feature is built — when its context is richest — this pipeline drafts a premium, on-brand enablement video and one-pager, quality-checks them (including a claim-check that won't ship an unsupported claim), routes them for human approval, then publishes to YouTube, the enablement hub, and Slack. Two directors (content + camera), dynamic on-brand assets, expressive voice, music, captions. This very video was generated by the pipeline.
